posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked:
Ameena:

If you're keeping your cards in your hand so other people can't see them, do you not have difficulty looking through them all easily on occasions where you've got a large hand? Mine are always just laid out in a line on the table, with another row above that for my in-play stuff.

I often split my large hand into cards I'm likely to play soon and cards I'm not, leaving the cards I'm not likely to play in a pile in my play area to grab from for discards. I'll occasionally revisit the piles when game state changes significantly, but I tend not to worry about it too much / spend too much time going through my hand.

(This is something I started to do to avoid anlaysis paralysis.   Plus it helps that I often know the cards well enough that, if there's something I suddenly need, I'll know it and can easily go retrieve it from the other pile.)

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked: I tend to hold my cards too, and then organise them as we play, thinking a couple of turns ahead and putting the ones I am about to play at the back (so I can simply flip the top card of my hand if I put them face down in a stack) and rearrange them when I draw a new one. If someone asks "Hey can you do X?" I either know I have that card as I was planning on playing it soon or I can look through the cards closest to me and see, I never need to go more than a few cards deep to answer their question.

posts.name: seesome
posts.cooked:
We always play with closed hands, even when playing with my daughter (12).

Table talk is encouraged; so if someone needs assistance, we can always say what we've got. 

However. the fun of playing closed hand is that when something bad pops up from the villain, one of us can go, "Don't worry, I've got this." and surprise the rest of the table with a great play.  That just isn't as cool when you know what cards other people are already holding.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: Well, you don't have to look at whatever cards they have laid out on the table ;). And it's possible they'll have something really convoluted in mind that you haven't thought of and which may involve other players doing stuff too (eg the Adept letting off a string of powers which involves letting someone else use something to help deal with the current problem). It's also easier if you are playing someone who supports other characters a lot to know what the other players are actually capable of - much easier to glance across at Unity's section of the table and see a bunch of bots sat there when you're trying to decide whom you should give a free card play to, for example ;). There is always plenty of talk in any game I play as we discuss what we should do - no-one ever tells anyone what they should be playing or anything and if they did I'd tell them off for it ;). When we've been playing at the London meets there are some people who seem to play with their hands hidden, but we tend to use a lot of decks that most other players present don't really know all that well anyway (owing to one of said players being a playtester who also happens to own all the Cauldron decks as well :D), so it probably wouldn't make much difference if we could see their cards or not ;).
